# zujson

zujson is a JSON parser and writer that converts between JSON and
ordinary R vectors and lists by a small, documented type mapping.

- It is built on [yyjson](https://github.com/ibireme/yyjson), whose
  sources it bundles, so it needs no system library and no package
  outside base R.
- No value changes type to fit a vector: an array of numbers and strings
  stays a list, unless you pass `simplify = "coerce"`.
- It reads and writes raw bytes as well as strings, which is how an HTTP
  body arrives and leaves.
- Every failure is a condition that inherits from `zujson_error`, so one
  handler catches them all.

## Installation

Install the released version from CRAN:

``` r

install.packages("zujson")
```

Or the development version from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zujson")
```

## Usage

``` r

library(zujson)
```

[`json_parse()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/reference/json_parse.md)
reads JSON into R. An object becomes a named list, and an array whose
elements share a type becomes an atomic vector:

``` r

str(json_parse('{"ok": true, "ids": [1, 2, 3], "next": null}'))
#> List of 3
#>  $ ok  : logi TRUE
#>  $ ids : int [1:3] 1 2 3
#>  $ next: NULL
```

[`json_write()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/reference/json_write.md)
goes the other way. A fully named list becomes an object, a vector an
array, and a length-one vector a bare value:

``` r

cat(json_write(list(query = "cats", limit = 10L, tags = c("a", "b"))))
#> {"query":"cats","limit":10,"tags":["a","b"]}
```

zujson also reads files and NDJSON, builds data frames from arrays of
records, and checks whether input is valid JSON; [Get
started](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/articles/zujson.html) shows
each of these.

## Learn more

- [Get started](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/articles/zujson.html)
  takes one response body through parsing, writing, raw bytes, errors
  and NDJSON.
- [Read a large API
  document](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/articles/kubernetes-openapi.html)
  works through the 3.3 MB Kubernetes API specification.
- [Handle malformed or untrusted
  input](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/articles/untrusted-input.html)
  covers the condition classes and the limits that bound the work.
- [Coming from
  jsonlite](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/articles/jsonlite.html)
  lists where the two packages give different results, and why.
- The
  [reference](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/reference/index.html)
  has the full type mapping in both directions.

zujson is narrower than
[jsonlite](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=jsonlite) by design; use
jsonlite when you need matrices, custom serializers or input too large
to hold in memory.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`json_parse()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/reference/json_parse.md)
  [`json_parse_raw()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/reference/json_parse.md)
  [`json_parse_file()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/reference/json_parse.md)
  : Parse JSON into R
- [`json_parse_ndjson()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/reference/json_parse_ndjson.md)
  [`json_write_ndjson()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/reference/json_parse_ndjson.md)
  [`json_write_ndjson_raw()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/reference/json_parse_ndjson.md)
  : Parse and write NDJSON
- [`json_validate()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/reference/json_validate.md)
  : Check whether input is valid JSON
- [`json_write()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/reference/json_write.md)
  [`json_write_raw()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/reference/json_write.md)
  : Serialize R as JSON
- [`zujson_info()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/reference/zujson_info.md)
  : Report what this build of zujson contains

# Articles

### Guides

- [Read a large API
  document](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/articles/kubernetes-openapi.md):

  Parse the 3.3 MB Kubernetes API specification from a file, query it,
  and turn its records into data frames.

- [Handle malformed or untrusted
  input](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/articles/untrusted-input.md):

  Catch what zujson raises, tell the failures apart, and know the limits
  that bound the work.

- [Coming from
  jsonlite](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/articles/jsonlite.md):

  Where zujson and jsonlite give different results for the same input,
  and the argument that closes each gap.

### Concepts

- [Testing and
  conformance](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujson/articles/testing.md):

  How zujson is tested, which parts of the JSON specification it
  accepts, and what it does where parsers disagree.
